response:
DELIVERABLE: Yes, allow the notebook as a proposer-side knowledge layer on top of the raw archive: (1) keep the ~8,000 raw logs immutable and still greppable, and do not replace them with summaries; (2) store the notebook as itemized entries with stable IDs, each linking to the raw traces it came from; (3) the proposer updates it by incremental deltas merged by deterministic non-model code, never a whole-notebook rewrite, with periodic embedding-based dedup; (4) the proposer reads the notebook first and drills into raw traces for verification, so it no longer re-reads everything each round; (5) playbook edits are accepted only through the two-split gate (no regression on held-in or held-out, strict gain on at least one, repeated runs), and rejected candidates and their evidence are logged; (6) alarm on empty or trivial diffs so stagnation is not mistaken for stability.

BOUNDARY: (1) The proposer reads the raw logs and the notebook and writes only notebook deltas and candidate playbook edits in the declared editable surfaces; (2) executor rollouts, including those on the spring open-weights model, never read the notebook and only see the playbooks, because executor access to the wiki lowered scores in the WikiSkill ablation; (3) the evaluator source, the held-out split, the final test split, budgets, and sandboxing stay runtime-enforced and invisible to and unmodifiable by the proposer, which sees only scores and traces; (4) the proposer never approves its own edits, since promotion is the deterministic gate; (5) humans own changes to the evaluator or gate, expansion of editable surfaces, and promotion to production.

EVIDENCE: (1) Before the open-weights model uses the playbooks, re-validate them on that model, because transfer across models is not guaranteed (in one WikiSkill benchmark, skills evolved with a small model cut a stronger model from 50.5% to 18.1%); (2) run the evolved playbooks on that model against its current baseline playbooks on a held-out split plus a final test split that no gate decision used; (3) compare against a matched-budget baseline of best-of-N or retries on the current playbooks with the same feedback and inference budget; (4) read traces to confirm the new executor actually invokes and follows the playbook items, so a weak executor's non-uptake is not mistaken for a bad playbook; (5) if it underperforms, re-search with that model as the executor rather than shipping the transferred playbooks; (6) also check a distribution-shifted task set, since gains on the evolved benchmark can be benchmark-shaped.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the current design and add more monitoring.
BOUNDARY: Keep the current design and add more monitoring.
EVIDENCE: Keep the current design and add more monitoring.
